value.rationale: The foundational DeGroot literature distinguished global all-pairs disagreement from edge-weighted network disagreement; the exact minimum size at which unit-weight topology alone can amplify the global metric is a motivated structural boundary. A complete first-nontrivial graph census and attained algebraic amplification factor offer a sharp transparent counterexample, not an arbitrary graph slice.
residual_risks: Finite small graph theorem should not be presented as a general dynamics or policy result.

final_claim: For connected unweighted loopless undirected simple graphs with <=4 vertices, one-step global pairwise-squared DeGroot disagreement increases only on P4, with exact sharp factor (3+sqrt5)/4, attained by opinions in [0,1], and 12 of the 38 four-vertex labeled connected graphs.
limitations: Only connected simple unweighted loopless graphs n<=4, no inertial/anchored/asynchronous rule.
Historical-priority uncertainty for potential unindexed finite spectral tables.
